body.x: KALMAN (CEO Jun-Ho Kim) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 at the K-Startup Pavilion.

KALMAN is a robotics company dedicated to addressing industrial challenges through innovative technologies. The company specializes in developing robots and systems to maintain high-value facilities, such as nuclear power plants, oil refineries, and gas processing facilities.
At CES 2025, KALMAN will present two advanced robotics solutions: the flying robot RADTECTOR-A, designed for radiation data acquisition, and the humanoid underwater robot ROBSTER-C.

RADTECTOR-A is a flying robot capable of acquiring and analyzing radiation data in and around nuclear power plants. This model is already operational in several domestic power plants, demonstrating its ability to meet stringent regulations and requirements for the nuclear industry. Notably, its performance remains stable even within facility interiors, earning high marks for practicality.

body.cap: ‘ROBSTER-C,’ a humanoid underwater robot for hazardous environments | Image provided by KALMAN

body.x: ROBSTER-C is a humanoid underwater robot addressing human divers’ safety concerns and operational challenges, such as accidents, limited working hours, and restricted access to hazardous areas. Designed to withstand radiation and operate efficiently at depths exceeding 100 meters, it is highly effective in radiation-exposed underwater facilities, intakes, ballast tanks, and offshore sites.

A KALMAN representative stated, “While we’ve focused on promoting our products and technology across Asia and Europe, CES 2025 marks our first opportunity to introduce the KALMAN brand to the North American market. We hope to connect with potential local partners and distribution channels to expand our business.”

The representative added, “Rising labor costs and increasingly stringent safety standards are accelerating automation trends in the plant sector. KALMAN’s robotics solutions are expected to gain significant attention globally, including in the U.S. Starting with these nuclear power plant-specific models, we plan to introduce a series of high-value-added plant robotics, further expanding our market influence.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally.
